protocol_checks.vulnerability_mechanism: CONFIRMED: SoupServer accepted a Range whose start was within the response but whose end exceeded total_length, then passed end-start+1 to soup_buffer_new_subbuffer() and later g_bytes_new_from_bytes(). The former had no bounds check; the latter can expose an out-of-bounds heap slice when GLib is built with G_DISABLE_CHECKS. GNOME issue 487, the PUBLISHED CVE record, and Red Hat's CWE-125 disposition describe this same mechanism.
protocol_checks.atomic_bic: CONFIRMED: 264eb7480e3a1c5762e4eb51f8273e6e438ff87b is the earliest public commit found by independent -S history for both soup_message_headers_get_ranges and handle_partial_get. Its diff first adds the unchecked explicit Range end and immediately uses it to size single- and multi-range response subbuffers.
protocol_checks.immediate_parent_absence: CONFIRMED: the sole parent 91d657fb12308d51608dd3f6b6c4b3fa6b117bee is present and verifiable; git grep of that tree finds neither soup_message_headers_get_ranges nor handle_partial_get, so the vulnerable source-to-sink mechanism is absent from the immediate parent.
protocol_checks.squash_member_decomposition: CONFIRMED: 264eb7480e3a1c5762e4eb51f8273e6e438ff87b has exactly one parent and records the surviving public SVN revision 1176. It is not a merge, move, revert, or later squash aggregate, and no finer earlier public member containing either mechanism symbol was found. The 2020 commit 4b43e158799689666bcbe186045ddee356601f1c only replaces SoupBuffer with GBytes while preserving the same unchecked slice and is not the BIC.
protocol_checks.release_membership: CONFIRMED: the BIC is an ancestor of tag 3.6.5, whose tree still has only the cur.start >= total_length check and both g_bytes_new_from_bytes sinks. Neither fix is in 3.6.5. Backport 9964993a32b2fa734a6b5ba2d465c2c14e22de17 is in 3.6.6, and direct fix 739bf7cb509c20141093d5a7f553007c8af81129 is in 3.7.1 and 3.7.2; those release trees bound or reject oversized ends.
protocol_checks.direct_fix: CONFIRMED: direct fix 739bf7cb509c20141093d5a7f553007c8af81129 changes the satisfiability check from start-only to start-or-end out of range and adds the invalid-end regression test. Its parent still contains the vulnerable start-only check and both sinks. Backport 9964993a32b2fa734a6b5ba2d465c2c14e22de17 has the identical stable patch-id a30364f2d7cc21bbe6fb14a19532f9f2a3dc7c6b.
protocol_checks.bic_only_ai_attribution: CONFIRMED: the BIC commit object names human author and committer Dan Winship <danw@src.gnome.org> on 2008-10-01 and contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI marker. Later commits and advisory metadata were not used for the AI-role judgment.

findings: CVE-2026-2443 is PUBLISHED, not rejected or withdrawn; Red Hat independently recognizes the CWE-125 while noting that its shipped GLib builds do not use G_DISABLE_CHECKS.
The primary correctly distinguishes the 2008 first-write BIC from the 2013 incomplete start-only validation and the 2020 GBytes refactor.
The primary's NOT_AI verdict and cited introducer, parent, direct fix, backport, and release boundary are independently reproduced.
